pr_comments:
> A test case that exercises the failure condition should be added.

Not the exercise I like, but will try :)
I've already started on that exercise but got distracted by something else so please tell me how far did you get.
@t8m, didn't start yet, had a lunch :)

After some fiddling with test_evp to add that testcase, I see it is much harder than expected. Especially given no documentation for these stitched ciphers. @mattcaswell could you give some hints how they should be used? I know I have to set the TLS1_AAD and the MAC_KEY but then I do not know how to get the whole ciphertext.

You need to set `OSSL_CIPHER_PARAM_AEAD_TLS1_AAD`, `OSSL_CIPHER_PARAM_AEAD_MAC_KEY` and  `OSSL_CIPHER_PARAM_TLS_VERSION`. Encryption is done "in place". You just call `EVP_EncryptUpdate`, and the output buffer should be the same as the input. Each record is a new `EVP_EncryptUpdate` call. The critical code that does all of this is here:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/f77208693ec3bda99618e6f76c0f8d279c0077bb/ssl/t1_enc.c#L137-L172
and here:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/f77208693ec3bda99618e6f76c0f8d279c0077bb/ssl/record/ssl3_record.c#L936-L1272
For expediency, this could be merged and a test provided in a followup PR.

issue_context.title: Wrong MAC calculation for certain plaintext lengths with AES128_CBC_SHA256 ciphersuites in TLS
issue_context.body:
When connecting to openssl server with a vanilla connection (i.e. no Encrypt then MAC, no Extended Master Secret) and TLS_*_AES_128_CBC_SHA256 ciphersuites, OpenSSL generates records with incorrect MAC, but only for certain sizes.
The ones I've tested were between 1000-1024 bytes and 2000-2048 bytes (inclusive). Of those 2032-2047 and 1008-1023 (inclusive) generate incorrect MAC values.

Reproducer:
```
cat > make-files.py << EOF
for i in range(1000, 1025):
    with open("data-{0}.txt".format(i), "wb+") as f:
        f.write(b"A" * (i-1) + b"\n")
EOF
python3 make-files.py
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa -keyout /tmp/localhost.key -out /tmp/localhost.crt -subj /CN=localhost -nodes -batch
openssl s_server -key /tmp/localhost.key -cert /tmp/localhost.crt -HTTP -cipher @SECLEVEL=0:AES128-SHA256
```
in another console:
```
git clone https://github.com/tomato42/tlsfuzzer
pushd tlsfuzzer
# won't be needed after https://github.com/tlsfuzzer/tlsfuzzer/pull/762 gets merged
git checkout length-testing
git clone https://github.com/tlsfuzzer/tlslite-ng .tlslite-ng
ln -s .tlslite-ng/tlslite tlslite
git clone https://github.com/tlsfuzzer/python-ecdsa .python-ecdsa
ln -s .python-ecdsa/src/ecdsa ecdsa
PYTHONPATH=. python3 scripts/test-lengths.py
```
(alternatively the server can be set up with either ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256 or DHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256 ciphersuite and tlsfuzzer script executed with the `-d` option)

While debugging it, @beldmit and me suspect the assembly `aesni_cbc_sha256_enc()` method.

yes, it's 3.0.0 only, 1.1.1k isn't affected

also setting `OPENSSL_ia32cap` to either `0x0:0x0` or masking the AES-NI bit makes the issue go away on master

My investigation so far:
1. it is not in aesni_cbc_sha256_enc() as masking SHAEXT and AVX bits does not make the issue go away but the aesni_cbc_sha256_enc() is not called in such case
2. it appears even in OPENSSL_NO_MULTIBLOCK build
git bisect tells me that the offending commit is 0d2bfe52bb
I'm afraid it just means that it's because of switching from legacy to provider in `crypto/evp/evp_enc.c`
Yes, the offending part of this commit is switching to provider code from legacy.

Current state: when https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/0d2bfe52bb7e839f7bddcdb1160c335f2994df2f is checked out, `providers/implementations/ciphers/cipher_aes_cbc_hmac_sha256_hw.c` implementation is broken but `crypto/evp/e_aes_cbc_hmac_sha256.c` is correct

s_client: `openssl s_client -connect localhost:4433 -no_etm -tls1_2 -cipher ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256`
After connection succeeds, request `GET /data-1019.txt HTTP/1.0`, where data-1019.txt is plain text file 1019 bytes length.

I get the following error on the s_client side:
